title: check: judge records by git history; warnings vs errors
description: Per DESIGN.md (2026-10-22): D6 a tier record is valid if its approver held authority at the commit that added it (approver stepping down voids nothing; only revocation voids); a tier record committed before its person file exists is ignored; a key listed in two files belongs to the file that listed it first; a revocation signed by a key later revoked counts if committed before that key's revocation; revocations are read from history so deleting the file does not undo one; void records and revoked-key-still-listed are reported, never fatal. check exits non-zero only on errors and prints warnings (D1, unendorsed emails, voided records, fetch age) separately. Replaces the hard failure at git-vouch:967-972.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture git registries cover each rule with real ssh-keygen signatures; approver removal no longer fails check; exit status distinguishes errors from warnings.
notes: Implemented in git-vouch: History/registry_history (linear order = git rev-list --topo-order --reverse HEAD; working tree is one pending version at index final; a non-git dir has only that version, so plain-dir tests keep snapshot semantics). check_registry: tier record judged by approver's claimed+valid tier at the commit that added its current content (History.added), recursion ends because claimed rank strictly falls; tier record committed before its person file -> void (warning); key in two files -> first listing commit owns, later lister is an error and dropped, same-commit ties keep the old current-key rule; every revocation version ever committed counts, processed in commit order, signer eligibility (key itself, subject's and anchors' unretired keys) taken from files at that commit, void if signer revoked in a strictly earlier commit, same-commit revocations all count; CheckResult gains warnings (revoked key still current). Errors only for working-tree versions; historical bad versions are silent. Tests: tests/test_check_history.py (13 tests, real git + ssh-keygen; snapshot-copy cross-checks). Open question: automation accountable still judged at the current tree (accountable stepping down = error).
